extra_brief:
India-specific guidance (established by the orchestrator this run — use it, and challenge it):

**The regulator's own line-wise register exists and is authoritative-ish.** PNGRB (Petroleum
and Natural Gas Regulatory Board) publishes a MONTHLY line-wise inventory of authorised
natural-gas pipelines: `https://pngrb.gov.in/data-bank/<YYYYMMDD>-NGPL-MIS-Report.pdf`
(latest edition 20260531). Printed page 2, "PHYSICAL PROGRESS REPORT OF NATURAL GAS
PIPELINE", is the only line-wise table. Per pipeline it gives: entity, authorisation date,
authorised length (km), authorised + design/determined capacity (MMSCMD), monthly gas
supplied, capacity utilisation, OPERATING length, UNDER-CONSTRUCTION length,
lowered/welded/hydrotested length, target completion date, and states traversed. It splits
pipelines into OPERATIONAL / PARTIALLY COMMISSIONED / UNDER CONSTRUCTION sections. This is
the regulator, so it is an origin INDEPENDENT of the GAIL / GSPL / IOCL annual reports.
Fetch it with curl and read it with `pdftotext -layout`; url_verifier will likely return
HTTP 200 + "value not found" on it (documented large-PDF false negative), so confirm values
locally and say so in your notes.

**IMPORTANT — it covers COMMON-CARRIER pipelines only.** Dedicated and tie-in lines (ONGC
trunk lines, Duliajan-Numaligarh, refinery feeders) are inside its grand totals but are NOT
itemised. If your pipeline is absent from the table, that is NOT evidence it does not exist —
it most likely means it is a dedicated line. Do not raise an existence concern on that basis
alone.

**GEM's India CapacityBcm/y appears to be DERIVED from PNGRB's authorised MMSCMD** via
MMSCMD x 365 / 1000. That reproduces the sheet value exactly to 2dp on ~20 rows (e.g. KG
Basin 16.0 -> 5.84, Dadri-Panipat 20.0 -> 7.30, Ennore-Tuticorin 84.7 -> 30.90). So if the
sheet's capacity disagrees with the CURRENT PNGRB edition, the likely story is a STALE
authorised capacity, not a unit error. Say which reading you land on.

**Authorisation date is NOT a commissioning year.** PNGRB's "Authorisation Date" is when the
regulator authorised the pipeline; it can precede first gas by a decade. Never propose
StartYear1 from an authorisation date. (Same class of error as dating a pipeline from its
gas field's discovery year.)

**"Partially commissioned" is a real regulatory category and it explains GEM's India row
pairs.** Several Indian pipelines are tracked in GEM as TWO rows — an `operating` row for
the commissioned portion and a `construction` row for the rest (Mehsana-Bhatinda,
Bhatinda-Gurdaspur, Mallavaram-Bhopal-Bhilwara-Vijaipur, Kochi-Koottanad-Bangalore-
Mangalore). PNGRB lists each as ONE authorised asset with an operating length AND an
under-construction length that sum to the authorisation. So such a pair is a GRANULARITY
difference, NOT a duplicate. Do not raise a duplicate concern on a pair like this; instead
check whether GEM's operating/under-construction SPLIT matches PNGRB's current numbers, and
flag the split if it does not.

**PNGRB reports HVJ + GREP + DVPL + VDPL as ONE combined system** (6,169 km authorised /
6,732 km operating), whereas GEM splits it across P0925 (HVJ), P0919 (DVPL-I), P3298
(DVPL-II), P3297 (GREP-I), P3299 (GREP-II) and possibly P0957. Again: granularity, not
error. Corroborate your row against the system total and say so; do not propose collapsing
GEM's rows.

**Diameter is the real gap.** Only 10 of 75 India gas rows carry a Diameter, and PNGRB's
table does NOT include diameter. Diameters live in PNGRB bid/tender documents and entity
maps (GAIL, GSPL, IOCL). A sourced diameter is high-value here.

Other Indian sources worth trying: GAIL / GSPL / GIGL / GITL / IGGL / IOCL annual reports
and investor presentations, PNGRB public notices and bid documents
(`pngrb.gov.in/pdf/public-notice/...`, `.../bid/...`), the Petroleum Planning & Analysis
Cell (PPAC) `ppac.gov.in`, and the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas annual report.
Regional-language sources are rarely needed; English coverage is good.
